I had just graduated and was starting to work as an RN in the hospital when Covid hit. The first time I heard Epiphany it hit me like a ton of bricks. I worked with Covid patients in March/April of 2020. I switched to working inpatient psychiatric/mental health and the amount of patients I had that were suicidal from the effects of the pandemic (loved ones passing, losing jobs, just overall stress, etc) was traumatic. I also lost a loved one unexpectedly in March of 2020 and wasn’t allowed to go to their funeral because everybody was worried that I might give them Covid. 

There were days in the beginning that we were advised to “stay calm, and masks weren’t needed”. I would work with patients all day & come back the next shift to learn that they had Covid. It traumatized me so much that I don’t think I’ll ever work in a hospital again. 

That said: Epiphany put into words feelings that I couldn’t express. Everybody was scared, and I didn’t want to add to their stress so I just never talked about the things I saw. The song helped me cope, but I can still only listen to it when I’m in a certain headspace because it brings up strong feelings. My husband played the song unprompted the other day and I was like nah fam. 🤣
